chunks: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated to us, and Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated to us, from his father, who said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him):

'Why were the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) called al-Hawariyyun?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the people, they were called Hawariyyun because they were tailors who cleansed clothes from dirt by washing, and it is a name derived from the bread called
And as for us, they were called Hawariyyun because they were pure in themselves and made others pure from the filth of sins through preaching and reminding.'

He said, so I said to him, 'Why were the Christians (al-Nasara) called al-Nasara?' He said, 'Because they are from a town called Nasirah in the land of Syria, where Mary and Jesus (peace be upon them) settled after their return from Egypt.'

key_terms.النَّصَارَى: Christians, derived from the town of Nasirah
key_terms.الْحَوَارِيُّونَ: The disciples of Jesus, literally meaning 'those who cleanse' or 'tailors'
key_terms.الْحُوَّارَى: A type of fine bread, source of the etymological root
key_terms.نَاصِرَةُ: A town in Syria where Mary and Jesus settled

ai.seo_question: What is the reason behind the names Hawariyyun and Nasara according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the popular etymology of 'Hawariyyun' as tailors who cleanse clothes and the Shia scholarly view that they were pure in themselves and cleansed others from sin through preaching. He attributes the name 'Nasara' to their settlement in the town of Nasirah in Syria, offering a geographical rather than purely linguistic explanation. This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on spiritual purity and active guidance as the true essence of the disciples' title.
